I will keep the farm simple and steady this year. In Quzhou County, the crop pattern I trust most is winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. I am 64, so I would not spread myself across too many crops or try anything complicated. Grain is easier for me to manage, easier to sell, and fits the local weather, machinery, and irrigation habits. I would stay with the varieties and field work I know, use improved or hybrid seed where it clearly helps yield and stability, and keep fertilizer and water at moderate levels so I do not waste money. For wheat, I would focus on steady nutrition, a few irrigations at key stages, and basic disease and weed control. After wheat harvest, I would seed maize quickly, keep the stubble and use no-tillage to save labor and time, then manage fertilizer, water, and pests in a straightforward way. My aim is not to chase the highest possible yield; it is to get a reliable harvest with work I can finish on time.
